intro: This is Michelin's pure comfort-food category: all eight spots are Bib Gourmand, each punching far above its shophouse price tag. Start with Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla on Chan Road, where restaurant-grade tao-toey fish lands in a humble roadside room, then Urai Braised Goose, which slow-braises a whole Teochew goose fresh every morning, and Thai Tham, a century-old shop in Phrang Phuthon where the eighty-something owner still ladles pork-brain soup at the stove herself.
quickAnswerHtml: This category gathers 8 Bib Gourmand Thai-Chinese restaurants from the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, led by Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla and its restaurant-grade tao-toey fish porridge on Chan Road.

blocks.html: This is Michelin's pure comfort-food category: all eight spots are Bib Gourmand, each punching far above its shophouse price tag. Start with Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla on Chan Road, where restaurant-grade tao-toey fish lands in a humble roadside room, then Urai Braised Goose, which slow-braises a whole Teochew goose fresh every morning, and Thai Tham, a century-old shop in Phrang Phuthon where the eighty-something owner still ladles pork-brain soup at the stove herself.

blocks.name: Baan Heng
blocks.descHtml:
Baan Heng is open daily 06:00–13:00 (some sources say it sells until 14:30, though the best dishes often sell out before then, so plan to go in the morning). The restaurant sits on Klang Mueang Road, right in the heart of Khon Kaen, a few minutes' drive from Bueng Kaen Nakhon or Khon Kaen railway station. The budget is very easy — around 100–250 THB per person, with rice congee starting at just 10 THB and most breakfast dishes running from the low tens up to just over a hundred baht.

The restaurant is walk-in only, no advance booking needed, with a contact number at 092-626-2236. Peak time is Saturday-Sunday mornings, when Khon Kaen locals and visitors alike pack the place for khai kratha egg skillet. If you don't want to wait, arrive before 9am. The most-ordered dishes are the khai kratha egg skillet, crispy-bottom Chinese sausage rice, and the Baan Heng sandwich. Before you leave, don't skip the souvenir corner — pick up Heng Nguan Heng Tra Tuek Chinese sausage and pork sausage, made in-house at the restaurant, or if you're already home and craving more, order long-distance through LINE @baanheng. Dress code is casual — it's a family restaurant with a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. Read the full review →
blocks.bestFor: A legendary Khon Kaen breakfast for khai kratha egg-skillet and homemade Chinese sausage fans and souvenir hunters
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Baan Heng official Facebook page

blocks.name: Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla
blocks.descHtml:
Real spend per person runs around THB 150-400, depending on which grade of fish you order — fish congee starts at THB 90-160, the tao tia and pickled-plum pomfret dishes are THB 350, and the pomfret fish congee is THB 500. There's no online booking — just walk in, or call ahead at 081-827-2381 / 02-211-0829. Open for dinner only, every day, from around 16:30; closing time varies by source, somewhere between 21:00-23:00, so call ahead if you're heading in late. The busiest stretch is 18:00-20:00 — go before 6pm or after 8pm if you'd rather skip the wait.

It's located on Chan Road near Saphan 2 (Thung Wat Don, Sathorn), which has no train station in walking distance — the BRT Chan Road stop is around 1.5km away. The most convenient option is a taxi from BTS Surasak or Chong Nonsi. If you're driving, park along the street or in the lot behind the restaurant. It's a shophouse with no air-con, so dress casual. One key tip: the pomfret dishes take a while to cook, so order that one first as soon as you sit down, then order the pork belly and glass noodles to snack on while you wait. If you'd rather stay in, you can order delivery through LINE MAN. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Chan Road near Saphan 2 (Thung Wat Don, Sathorn)
blocks.signature: Tao tia fish congee — restaurant-grade Chinese fish at shophouse prices on Chan Road
blocks.bestFor: Fish lovers who want restaurant-grade fish congee in a shophouse setting, an easy dinner with family or friends
blocks.zone: Chan Road near Saphan 2 (Thung Wat Don, Sathorn)
blocks.hours: Dinner only, every day, from ~16:30 (closing time varies by so

blocks.name: Hok Kee Lao
blocks.descHtml:
Hok Kee Lao is in Takua Pa, near the big market, across from the Esso station — easy to find. Prices run about THB 101–250 per person, easy on the wallet for a Bib Gourmand restaurant, but according to MICHELIN the restaurant only takes cash, so bring enough. It's open every day, split into two sittings: 10:30-13:30 and 16:30-21:30. The restaurant closes for a break from 13:30-16:30 — don't show up then, you'll find it shut.

It's mostly walk-in, but if you're coming as a large group or visiting for a busy holiday lunch, it's worth calling ahead at +66 76 421 938 or the backup number 081-891-2296 — the restaurant only takes bookings by phone. There's an air-conditioned room upstairs, good for larger family groups. The most convenient way there is by car — it's not far up Phetkasem Road from Khao Lak, so you can stop for a meal and then walk around Takua Pa Old Town afterward. Dress is casual, no rules there. The easiest time to go is a weekday dinner — the evening sitting runs until 9:30pm. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Soy-braised free-range chicken with water spinach
mustOrder: Soy-braised free-range chicken with water spinach
Loaded tofu (fried tofu with minced pork and shrimp)
Crab noodle rolls (fried minced pork and shrimp)
blocks.bestFor: Family gatherings/large groups and drivers touring Khao Lak-Takua Pa Old Town who want old-school Chinese food at prices in the low hundreds
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Hok Kee Lao official Facebook page

blocks.name: Hong Seng
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per person runs about THB 251–500 and up — most vegetable dishes and fried items are in the low hundreds, but the grilled giant river prawns are priced by size, so the bigger the prawn, the higher the bill, and the restaurant is cash only — worth remembering, so withdraw cash before you go. Booking is by calling the restaurant directly at 02-583-8631 or 02-583-7654 — they manage their own queue entirely, with no online booking system available.

The time to plan around carefully is weekdays, since the restaurant only serves lunch, opening around 10:00–10:30 (sources differ) and closing at 2pm sharp. On Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays it stays open until 4pm. The riverside wooden terrace tables are always the first to go on weekends, so arrive before noon if you want the Chao Phraya view. There are three ways to get there — take the Pink Line to Pak Kret Junction station (PK06) and walk about 20 minutes or grab a 5-minute motorbike taxi; drive and park in the public space under the Rama IV Bridge; or take a boat straight to the Pak Kret pier next to the restaurant, exactly as MICHELIN itself recommends. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Pak Kret riverside (foot of Rama IV Bridge, next to Pak Kret municipal pier), Nonthaburi
blocks.signature: Grilled giant river prawns with spicy seafood dipping sauce
mustOrder: Grilled giant river prawns with spicy seafood dipping sauce
Mini deep-fried crab meat rolls wrapped in tofu skin
Stir-fried bitter gourd with salted fish
Kale stems stir-fried with prawn claws
Mango sticky rice with coconut milk
blocks.bestFor: A riverside lunch with the family — grilled giant river prawns on the wooden terrace of a 60-plus-year-old Pak Kret institution
blocks.zone: Pak Kret riverside (foot of Rama IV Bridge, next to Pak Kret municipal pier), Nonthaburi

blocks.name: Pae
blocks.descHtml:
Pae Pochana is a genuine budget-friendly Bib Gourmand — average spend is THB 250–500 a head, with most standout dishes at THB 160–240 and only the fried sun-dried snakehead fish reaching THB 410. No advance booking needed, since the shop is mainly walk-in. If you want to call ahead and check, use 082-250-9191 (a third-party AutoReserve listing exists, but calling direct is more reliable). The one thing to plan around is timing — the shop is open every day but sells only at lunch, 09:00–14:30, and the popular dishes often sell out by around 1pm, with weekend waits running up to 1.5 hours. The safe formula is to arrive before 11:00.

It sits inside Rahaeng Market, a century-old wooden canal-side market in Lat Lum Kaeo, Pathum Thani. There's no train line out here, so you'll need to drive or grab a ride, in exchange for eating canal-side on the wooden walkway of an old market. One thing to watch for: the shop closes about 2 unannounced days a month, announced on its Facebook page — check the page every time before you head out. Read the full review →

mustOrder: Minced featherback fish and pork wrapped in tofu sheets (moo song khreung/moo jaw)

blocks.name: Thai Tham
blocks.descHtml:
Thai Tham is one of the easiest restaurants on the MICHELIN list on your wallet — snacks start at 25 baht for taro pork balls, about 30 baht a skewer for grilled liver sausage, while the signature mixed offal-and-brain soup runs about 120 baht a bowl. Per-head budget, according to Wongnai, is around 101–250 baht for a full meal. No reservation needed, just walk in and sit down, or call 02-221-7612 to ask ahead — and note the shop takes cash only.

What you need to plan around is "timing" more than the queue. The shop is open Monday–Saturday 07:00–14:00, closed Sunday and public holidays. The stewed pig's brain is made fresh every morning and is limited — on busy days it typically sells out by early afternoon, and the shop itself recommends coming before noon. For a sure bet, go in the morning to late morning. Getting there is easy via MRT Sam Yot station, then about a 10-minute walk into the Phraeng Phuthon area. The shop is at 28/1 Phraeng Phuthon Rd, San Chao Pho Suea, Phra Nakhon — a great breakfast stop before a full day exploring the Old Town. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Stewed pig's brain soup made fresh every morning, by the octogenarian owner of a century-old shop in Phraeng Phuthon
mustOrder: Stewed pig's brain soup (fresh every morning ~THB 120)
blocks.bestFor: A light-budget breakfast-brunch stop before you explore the Old Town, and a spot for hard-to-find dishes like century-old pig's brain soup
blocks.hours: Mon–Sat 07:00–14:00; closed Sun and public holidays
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Thai Tham official Facebook page

blocks.name: Urai Braised Goose
blocks.descHtml:
The budget here is light — braised goose small plate THB 250 for 1–2 people, medium THB 420, large THB 840, rice THB 10 a plate, free Chinese tea. All in, that's about THB 150–300 per person and you're full, but bring cash since the restaurant is cash-only. No reservations under any circumstances — it's walk-in only. There's a phone number, 02-221-4413, but it can't be used to book a table, so the whole game comes down to timing your visit.

The restaurant runs two shifts: morning 10:00–13:00 (Sundays until noon only) and evening 16:00–19:00, but the goose typically sells out before closing. The morning shift usually sells out around noon and the queue starts stretching out from 12:30 even on weekdays. The safest time to go is right at opening, 10:00 sharp. If you're set on trying the braised goose intestines, you need to pick either a Wednesday or a Saturday — that's the only time it's available. Getting there is easy: take the MRT to Wat Mangkon station, then walk about 7 minutes. The restaurant is at 935 Song Wat Road, Samphanthawong, so you can keep exploring Song Wat–Yaowarat on foot afterward. Read the full review →

faq.q: Which Thai-Chinese spot here should I try first?
faq.a: Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla on Chan Road in Bangkok is the first stop, serving restaurant-grade tao-toey fish porridge in a plain roadside shophouse for far less than you would expect.

faq.q: Are there any Michelin-starred restaurants in this group?
faq.a: No, all eight are Bib Gourmand, Michelin's mark for great food at a friendly price, which makes them ideal when you want something excellent without a long-advance booking.

faq.q: Which dishes did Michelin call out by name?
faq.a: Pae in Pathum Thani earns a direct nod for its moo song khruang, minced featherback fish and pork wrapped in tofu skin, while Thai Tham is known for its pork-brain broth simmered fresh each morning.

faq.q: Where do I go for a proper braised goose?
faq.a: Urai Braised Goose in Bangkok braises a whole goose each morning in a long-aged master stock and serves it Teochew-style over rice.

faq.q: Which provinces do these restaurants cover?
faq.a: Most sit in Bangkok, including Hia Wan, Urai and Thai Tham, with the rest spread across Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani, Nakhon Ratchasima, Khon Kaen and Phang-Nga.
